docs.title: Bondi Beach
docs.text: Bondi is Sydney's most famous beach — a kilometre of golden sand backed by cafés, shops, and the iconic Icebergs pool.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Bondi draws locals and visitors year-round for swimming, surfing, and the scenic coastal walk to Coogee. The beach is patrolled by lifeguards and easily reached by bus from the city.

docs.title: Key information
docs.text: Patrolled Yes — follow flag warnings Best for Swimming, surfing, coastal walk Getting there Bus 333 from Circular Quay (~40 min) Facilities Showers, changerooms, cafés, lifeguard tower

docs.title: Is Bondi Beach free?
docs.text: Yes. Access to the beach is free. Paid parking and some pool areas (e.g. Icebergs) have separate fees.

docs.title: Can you swim at Bondi year-round?
docs.text: Yes, but winter water temperatures are cooler. Always swim between the flags when lifeguards are on duty.

docs.title: How long is the Bondi to Coogee walk?
docs.text: About 6 km, allow 2–3 hours with stops.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text: Getting around Sydney is straightforward once you know the Opal system and key ferry and train routes.

docs.title: Opal card
docs.text:
Opal is Sydney's integrated ticketing system for trains, buses, ferries, and light rail. Tap on and off at every trip.

Airport trains

The train to Sydney Airport carries a station access fee on top of the normal fare.
